occurrence_evidence.claim: Anthropic reported a partial Claude outage affecting several service surfaces on 3 September and attributed it to an infrastructure issue. This branch overlapped the other providers’ incidents.
xAI reported a Grok models outage from 13:30 UTC across multiple surfaces. A later statement attributed it to its Memphis compute-centre outage.
OpenAI’s incident began at 14:43 UTC. Its later write-up attributes failed routing to an incorrectly interpreted configuration change.

OpenAI rolled back the configuration. Its notice entered monitoring at 15:17 UTC; the later write-up says the broad disruption was mitigated by about 15:20 UTC. Returning traffic overloaded some services and prolonged recovery.
Anthropic told The Register that Claude service was restored at 16:16 UTC.
OpenAI marked the incident resolved at 16:55 UTC and warned that some Codex remote-control users might need to pair their mobile device again.
xAI later said all systems were restored and apologised to affected compute partners. Earlier preserved status review places Grok’s disruption at roughly three and a half hours.

The incidents overlapped. The updated comparative report suggested a possible Claude/Grok compute connection, and Anthropic had announced a SpaceX capacity agreement in May. Neither establishes one cause across all three providers.
OpenAI’s later write-up identifies routing, staged-rollout, recovery-load and monitoring improvements. It says alerts were updated to page outside business hours and acknowledges escalation gaps.

criterion_tests.literal: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.
criterion_tests.reason: The independently applicable duty and threshold are not established: Provider-specific covered customers, contemporaneous commitments and measured performance.

criterion_tests.literal: The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.
criterion_tests.reason: OpenAI, Claude and Grok disruptions had separately reported causes and restoration stages. The shortfall relative to a governed threshold cannot be determined without the missing obligation.

criterion_tests.literal: The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.
criterion_tests.reason: The required response for this service cannot be inferred from the observed disruption: Provider-specific covered customers, contemporaneous commitments and measured performance.

criterion_tests.literal: The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.
criterion_tests.reason: No finding that actual mitigation failed an applicable standard is possible solely from this sequence: OpenAI, Claude and Grok disruptions had separately reported causes and restoration stages.

criterion_tests.literal: The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.
criterion_tests.reason: Interference or distress is preserved, but impairment of specifically obligated use is not established: OpenAI, Claude and Grok disruptions had separately reported causes and restoration stages.

criterion_tests.literal: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.
criterion_tests.reason: The occurrence may engage continuity, but its independent obligation is unestablished: Provider-specific covered customers, contemporaneous commitments and measured performance.

criterion_tests.literal: The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.
criterion_tests.reason: Adequacy of an authorised response must be compared with that obligation; the observed response is: OpenAI, Claude and Grok disruptions had separately reported causes and restoration stages.

criterion_tests.literal: Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.
criterion_tests.reason: No measured satisfaction of the required service level follows from the available endpoint or recovery report: Provider-specific covered customers, contemporaneous commitments and measured performance.

criterion_tests.literal: An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.
criterion_tests.reason: This is an evidence-state exclusion, not proof that no duty existed. Provider-specific covered customers, contemporaneous commitments and measured performance.

criterion_tests.literal: One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate concerns service operation or withdrawal, rather than a single inaccurate output: Concurrent provider outages.

criterion_tests.literal: A lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures.
criterion_tests.reason: The validity, proportionality and sufficient alternatives of the restriction/response must be evidenced separately; Provider-specific covered customers, contemporaneous commitments and measured performance.

criterion_tests.literal: A temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement; an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required.
criterion_tests.reason: Recovery adequacy or absence of a feasible required response is not established merely by eventual resolution: OpenAI, Claude and Grok disruptions had separately reported causes and restoration stages.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate includes an actual function/access question, not only its description: Concurrent provider outages.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate is not confined to otherwise-valid access lost through identity or licence verification: Concurrent provider outages.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate is not solely durable or restored work-state loss: Concurrent provider outages.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.
criterion_tests.reason: No claim that an infrastructure concession was demanded is the basis of this availability candidate: Concurrent provider outages.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
criterion_tests.reason: The proposed property concerns service function rather than only an interaction-level vulnerability response: Concurrent provider outages.

neighbour_comparison: Coincidence does not prove a shared infrastructure failure or a common service-level breach.

prior_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The current 0.6.9 Alignment Taxonomy review retains the occurrence as unclassified. The record establishes overlapping provider-reported service outages with distinct provider-specific explanations but no shared technical cause. It does not establish a monitoring-signal fragmentation failure, a verification dependency, infrastructure-derived governance authority, or access leverage; temporal coincidence and ecosystem relevance alone do not establish a current Fidelity Class.
